Supreme Court of India

facts: The appeal in question tell the tale of a young girl dying out of burn injuries.

On the basis of the fardbeyan of the informant Phulamati the mother of the deceased, that the appellant alongwith other members of the family on the night of 06/07 March 1991 had set her daughter on fire and on having such information the informant alongwith PWs 3,4 and 7 reached the Muhalla and found that the daughter was lying injured due to burn injuries.

The First Information Report recorded that the daughter of the informant disclosed that her husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law and other family members forcibly poured kerosene oil on her body and lighted, on account of which her entire body was burnt.
issues: Whether the demand for dowry was interpolated and inserted in the FIR
Whether the conviction under Section 304B can be converted to Section 302 IPC
petitioner_arguments: The Court having recorded a finding that the demand for dowry was interpolated and inserted in the FIR, virtually in a different handwriting, which was done subsequently it is submitted that, it is unsafe to rely on the informant PW5 and the Prosecution case is fit to be rejected outright

Since the prosecution failed to prove the charges against any of the accused and that the conviction and sentence under the aforesaid charges including that of the appellant having been set aside, the conviction of the appellant under S. 302 IPC is bad in law and untenable
respondent_arguments: The allegation with regard to demand of dowry was inserted subsequently, but it cannot be alleged that such an allegation was made after interpolation
There is no evidence whatsoever that prior to the date of occurrence, there was any demand for dowry by the accused persons
court_reasoning: The High Court also in no uncertain terms recorded that the statement of Mr. Verma stands justified by reason of interpolation on the First Information Report
We are at a loss to find such an omission on the part of the High Court on such a vital issue
holding: The criminal appeal was partly allowed so far as the appellant Nos. 1,2 and 4 were concerned but appellant No.3 being the husband (Arvind Singh) subject to the modification of conviction was dismissed
In the result the criminal appeal was partly allowed so far as the appellant Nos. 1,2 and 4 were concerned
